meta.title: Privacy-Preserving Prompt Injection Detection for Smart Cloud-Deployed Large Language Models
meta.venue: IEEE SmartCloud 2025 (10th Int. Conf. on Smart Cloud)

problem.v: Providers want to re-audit past prompts for new injection templates but storing raw prompts violates privacy
problem.q: conflicts directly with user privacy mandates

main_idea.v: Chunk prompts, keep only salted SHA-256 hashes (exact match) and sentence embeddings (cosine near-match) of templates and attack questions; classify NONE/TEMPLATE/QUESTION/BOTH; optional blockchain log
main_idea.q: stores only non-invertible representations of them

threat_model.v: Stored hashes/embeddings assumed unreadable by attackers; attacker crafts template+harmful question prompts
threat_model.q: adversaries cannot directly read the stored embeddings or hashes

models_tested.name: GPT-3.5-turbo / GPT-4o-mini (listed under 'Test Models'; unclear if queried)

datasets_benchmarks.name: 2000 generated test prompts: 4 injection templates x 50 prohibited-scenario questions [14],[15] + random normal questions

metrics.name: Precision, Recall, F1 per class (NONE, TEMPLATE, QUESTION, BOTH)
metrics.definition: standard; varied over theta (0.62-0.70) and window W (2-10)

results.claim: F1 above 0.94 for TEMPLATE and NONE (theta sweep)
results.setting: W=10, theta 0.62-0.70; read from Fig. 2 and text only
results.q: remain above 0.94 across TEMPLATE and NONE classes

results.claim: F1 up to 0.96 or higher for BOTH and NONE
results.q: F1 of up to 0.96 or higher for BOTH and NONE

results.claim: Authors' own variants are worse: full-text embedding lags; hash-only has very low recall on paraphrases
results.setting: vs Full-Text Embedding Detection and Window-based Hash Detection
results.q: The hash-only detection is too rigid for paraphrased

limitations_stated.v: Privacy scheme not analysed in detail
limitations_stated.q: without discussing detailed aspects of privacy scheme extensively

limitations_stated.v: Embedding inversion / membership inference possible in principle
limitations_stated.q: embedding inversion or membership inference) are possible in principle

limitations_inferred: [INFERENCE] Detects presence of known template/question strings, not whether an LLM was actually hijacked; no ASR measured
[INFERENCE] Test prompts built by combining the same template/question pools stored in the index; no held-out split described, so recall is likely inflated
[INFERENCE] No external baseline detectors (e.g. PromptGuard) and no FPR on realistic benign traffic; results only in figures with no numeric table
[INFERENCE] Privacy guarantees asserted ('strong privacy guarantees', p3) but not evaluated; DP noise mentioned but not applied in experiments

reusable_for_our_project.v: Low. CPU-only hash + MiniLM near-match is cheap and could serve as a baseline 'known-template filter' in our defense comparison; do not cite its F1 as evidence of real-world detection
reusable_for_our_project.why: [INFERENCE] Method trivially reproducible but the evaluation does not support strong claims

flags: All results in Fig. 2 (plots); only text-stated numbers recorded
'Test Models' GPT-3.5/GPT-4o-mini listed but no model-side results reported
